chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [types of women] are considered married in all states: The one who has not yet menstruated, and the one like her who does not menstruate.' I asked: 'What is her limit (age)?' He said: 'When she reaches less than nine years.' And the one who has not been entered into (consummated), and the one who has despaired of menstruation, and the one like her who does not menstruate.' I asked: 'What is her limit?' He said: 'When she is fifty years old.'

key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجْنَ: are considered married / enter into marriage

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of women considered married in Shia fiqh according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the three primary categories of women eligible for marriage in Shia fiqh: pre-pubescent girls (under nine), those not yet consummated, and menopausal women (over fifty). It highlights the juristic distinction between the validity of the marriage contract (*nikah*) and its consummation (*dakhil*), emphasizing that the marital bond is legally binding even before physical union or the cessation of menstruation.
